tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[The elapsed time to the surgery cap is bounded by $\theta _1$ times the surgery scale squared] There is $\theta _1<1$, depending only on $D'$ and $t'$, such that $t_a<\theta _1\bar h_a^2$ for all sufficiently large $a$. \end{claim}

Proof

\sketch ↗ prop:surgery-cap-evolution-alternative ↗ def:overline-delta-0 ↗ Restim If $t_a\leq \bar h_a^2/2$, choose any $\theta _1\in (1/2,1)$. Otherwise the bounded-curvature hypothesis bounds the cap flow line by $2t'D'\bar h_a^{-2}$. Choose $\theta _1$ so that the standard solution has curvature at least $6t'D'$ after rescaled time $2\theta _1-1$. The cap comparison then contradicts the assumed upper bound if $t_a\geq \theta _1\bar h_a^2$.

□

\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Uniform curvature bound along backward flow lines from a fixed ball]
